title: The Monkey's Paw
author: W. W. Jacobs
note: Abridged radio adaptation for a ~5-minute drama. Dialogue is Jacobs's own words, cut and occasionally joined across a few lines of the original; narration is shortened from his sentences. Audio tags in [brackets] are direction, not spoken.

characters.name: Narrator
characters.description: Older British male storyteller, low and unhurried, warm at first and growing quietly ominous; clear diction for radio.

characters.name: Mr White
characters.description: Elderly British man around seventy, thin and slightly reedy voice, amiable and curious, later shaken and frightened.

characters.name: Mrs White
characters.description: Elderly British woman around sixty-five, warm and dry-witted, later raw with grief and feverish hope.

characters.name: Herbert
characters.description: British man in his twenties, bright, teasing and quick, with an easy laugh.

characters.name: Sergeant-Major Morris
characters.description: Burly British ex-soldier in his fifties, gravelly and weathered, guarded, speaks slowly when serious.

characters.name: The man from Maw and Meggins
characters.description: Formal British clerk in his forties, nervous and halting, uncomfortable delivering bad news.

scenes.title: The paw
scenes.ambience: wind and rain against windows, a crackling fire in a small parlour

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Without, the night was cold and wet, but in the small parlour of Laburnam Villa the blinds were drawn and the fire burned brightly. Old Mr White and his son Herbert were at chess, while Mrs White knitted placidly by the fire.

lines.speaker: mr-white
lines.text: [cheerfully] Hark at the wind. I should hardly think that he'd come to-night.

lines.speaker: herbert
lines.text: [dryly] Mate.

lines.speaker: mrs-white
lines.text: [soothingly] Never mind, dear; perhaps you'll win the next one.
lines.sfx_after: a garden gate bangs shut, then heavy footsteps on a wet path

lines.speaker: herbert
lines.text: There he is.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sergeant-Major Morris was a tall, burly man, beady of eye. At the third glass of whiskey his eyes got brighter, and he began to talk.

lines.speaker: mr-white
lines.text: What was that you started telling me the other day about a monkey's paw or something, Morris?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: [hastily] Nothing. Leastways nothing worth hearing.

lines.speaker: mrs-white
lines.text: [curiously] Monkey's paw?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: [low] To look at, it's just an ordinary little paw, dried to a mummy. It had a spell put on it by an old fakir. He wanted to show that fate ruled people's lives, and that those who interfered with it did so to their sorrow. Three separate men could each have three wishes from it.

lines.speaker: herbert
lines.text: [teasing] Well, why don't you have three, sir?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: [quietly] I have.

lines.speaker: mrs-white
lines.text: And has anybody else wished?

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: [gravely] The first man had his three wishes. I don't know what the first two were, but the third was for death. That's how I got the paw.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Suddenly he threw it upon the fire. White, with a slight cry, stooped down and snatched it off.

lines.speaker: morris
lines.text: [solemnly] Better let it burn. If you keep it, don't blame me for what happens. Hold it up in your right hand and wish aloud, but I warn you of the consequences.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When their guest had gone, the old man took the paw from his pocket and eyed it dubiously.

lines.speaker: herbert
lines.text: [laughing] Well, wish for two hundred pounds, then; that'll just do it.

lines.speaker: mr-white
lines.text: [distinctly] I wish for two hundred pounds.
lines.sfx_after: a loud dramatic crash of piano chords

lines.speaker: mr-white
lines.text: [shuddering] It moved. As I wished, it twisted in my hand like a snake.

lines.speaker: herbert
lines.text: Well, I don't see the money, and I bet I never shall.

scenes.title: The visitor
scenes.ambience: quiet daytime house interior, a clock ticking, faint birds outside
scenes.music_mood: cold, still, a single low note of dread

lines.speaker: herbert
lines.text: [laughing] Well, don't break into the money before I come back.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Herbert went off to his work at Maw and Meggins. That afternoon, as Mr and Mrs White sat at dinner, a stranger in a silk hat of glossy newness paused three times at the gate. The fourth time he flung it open and walked up the path.
lines.sfx_after: a garden gate creaks open, slow footsteps on a path

lines.speaker: maw-meggins-man
lines.text: [hesitant] I... was asked to call. I come from Maw and Meggins.

lines.speaker: mrs-white
lines.text: [breathless] Is anything the matter? Has anything happened to Herbert? What is it? What is it?

lines.speaker: maw-meggins-man
lines.text: I'm sorry...

lines.speaker: mrs-white
lines.text: [wildly] Is he hurt?

lines.speaker: maw-meggins-man
lines.text: [quietly] Badly hurt, but he is not in any pain.

lines.speaker: mrs-white
lines.text: [relieved] Oh, thank God! Thank God for that! Thank...

lines.speaker: maw-meggins-man
lines.text: [low] He was caught in the machinery.

lines.speaker: mr-white
lines.text: [dazed] Caught in the machinery. Yes. He was the only one left to us. It is hard.

lines.speaker: maw-meggins-man
lines.text: [uneasy] I was to say that Maw and Meggins disclaim all responsibility. They admit no liability at all, but in consideration of your son's services, they wish to present you with a certain sum as compensation.

lines.speaker: mr-white
lines.text: [whispers] How much?

lines.speaker: maw-meggins-man
lines.text: Two hundred pounds.
lines.sfx_after: a heavy body falls onto a wooden floor

scenes.title: The knocking
scenes.ambience: a silent house at night, a clock ticking, a cold draught
scenes.music_mood: dark, sparse, rising dread, ends in silence

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the huge new cemetery, some two miles distant, the old people buried their dead, and came back to a house steeped in shadow and silence. A week after, old Mr White woke in the night and found himself alone. Mrs White was at the window, weeping.

lines.speaker: mrs-white
lines.text: [crying out] The paw! The monkey's paw! The other two wishes. We've only had one. Go down and get it quickly, and wish our boy alive again.

lines.speaker: mr-white
lines.text: [aghast] Good God, you are mad! He has been dead ten days, and besides he... I could only recognize him by his clothing. If he was too terrible for you to see then, how now?

lines.speaker: mrs-white
lines.text: [fierce] Bring him back. Do you think I fear the child I have nursed? Wish!

lines.speaker: mr-white
lines.text: [faltering] It is foolish and wicked.

lines.speaker: mrs-white
lines.text: [shouting] Wish!

lines.speaker: mr-white
lines.text: [trembling] I wish my son alive again.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [slowly] The candle flickered and expired. They lay silently listening to the ticking of the clock. He went down for a candle, and at the foot of the stairs a knock, so quiet and stealthy as to be scarcely audible, sounded on the front door.
lines.sfx_after: one quiet, stealthy knock on a heavy wooden front door

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He fled back to his room. A third knock sounded through the house.
lines.sfx_after: a loud knock echoing through an empty house

lines.speaker: mrs-white
lines.text: [screaming] It's Herbert! It's Herbert!

lines.speaker: mr-white
lines.text: [hoarse whisper] What are you going to do?

lines.speaker: mrs-white
lines.text: [struggling] It's my boy; it's Herbert! Let go. I must open the door. I'm coming, Herbert; I'm coming.

lines.speaker: mr-white
lines.text: [desperate] For God's sake don't let it in!
lines.sfx_after: frantic loud knocking on a front door, a door chain rattling and a bolt scraping

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [urgent] He was on his hands and knees, groping wildly on the floor for the paw. He heard the creaking of the bolt as it came slowly back, and at the same moment he found the monkey's paw, and frantically breathed his third and last wish.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: [quietly] The knocking ceased suddenly. A cold wind rushed up the staircase, and a long loud wail of disappointment and misery from his wife gave him courage to run down to her side. The street lamp flickering opposite shone on a quiet and deserted road.
